about.title: Murrieta Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Murrieta has grown into a city of nearly 110,000 people, and most of that growth shows up in shopping centers, apartment communities, medical offices, and parking lots along Murrieta Hot Springs Road, Clinton Keith Road, Whitewood Road, and Winchester Road. Every one of those properties has someone responsible for keeping it reasonably safe. When a spill sits uncleaned, a walkway stays cracked, or a stairwell light goes dark for weeks, the person who falls is left sorting out medical bills and missed shifts. Under California law, a property owner is generally answerable when they knew, or reasonably should have known, about a hazard and did nothing to repair it or warn about it. Proving that usually comes down to evidence that disappears fast: the puddle gets mopped, the incident report gets filed away, and the surveillance footage gets overwritten. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that links injured people in Murrieta and the rest of Riverside County with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your claim recovers something.

whyChoose.title: Why Murrieta Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Notice is the whole fight
items.desc: California asks whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can push for cleaning logs, prior complaints, and maintenance records that show how long the problem sat there.

items.title: Video is erased quickly
items.desc: Most stores and apartment complexes keep surveillance for only days or weeks. Getting a preservation letter out early can be the difference between a clear record of the fall and no record at all.

items.title: Deadlines and shared blame
items.desc: You generally have two years to file, and far less time if a city or county property is involved. California's pure comparative fault rule also means you can still recover even if you were partly at fault, with your share reduced accordingly.

items.question: I fell on a cracked sidewalk in a Murrieta city park. Is the deadline different?
items.answer: Yes. Claims against a public entity such as the City of Murrieta or Riverside County must go through a government claim process with a much shorter window than the usual two years. Missing that step can end the case before it starts. If you suspect public property was involved, do not wait to speak with an attorney.

items.question: The store manager says I was looking at my phone. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: Not by itself. California follows pure comparative fault, so if a jury decided you were partly responsible, your recovery would be reduced by that percentage rather than eliminated. The owner still has to answer for a hazard they knew about or should have caught.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall in Murrieta?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if the pain seems manageable. Then photograph the hazard, your footwear, and the surroundings, and write down the names of anyone who saw it happen. Ask the property in writing to preserve any surveillance video, because footage is routinely overwritten. A connected attorney can send that request formally.
